steps.title: The Character studio
steps.body: The Characters workspace dresses minifigures (hair, face, outfit, colors, gear) and animates them with keyframe clips. The hero and every neighbour are characters.

steps.title: A new character
steps.body: Start from one of v68's presets: + New character shows a picture of each one; click the one you want. The copy is yours to change; presets themselves stay as they are.
steps.task: Click + New character, then click a preset’s picture.

steps.title: Change the look
steps.body: The properties on the right change every part of the look; the preview updates at once. Each change is one undo step.
steps.task: Rename the character or change a color.

steps.title: The player character
steps.body: One character is the hero the player controls. “Make player character” (or Project tab › Hero) picks it.
steps.task: Make your character the player character.

steps.title: Animation clips
steps.body: Clips are keyframe animations on a timeline: a lane per joint (track), keys (◆) that say where the joint is at a moment, and markers that send events, play sounds or start cinematics. Between two keys the joint moves smoothly. Keys 1–4 play the hero’s emotes in Play.
steps.task: Make a new clip: Clips › + New (left).

doItForMe.say: Click + New next to Clips (left). The new clip opens with an empty timeline under the preview.

how: In the panel on the left, scroll down to Clips and click + New (right of the word Clips). A clip called New clip is made and opens: the timeline appears under the preview.

steps.title: Animate the clip
steps.body: Animating means adding keys: at a moment of the clip, set where a joint is. Here the right arm goes up at 1 second and back down at the end, so the clip lifts the arm and drops it again, over and over (Loop).
steps.task: Make the right arm rise and fall: add a Right arm · z track and a key at 1 s with the arm up (value 2.6).
how: Your new clip is open (highlighted under Clips, left); its timeline is under the preview, with the time at 0.00 / 2.00 s.
In the timeline tools, open + Track… and pick Right arm · z (it lifts the arm out to the side). A lane appears with a key ◆ at 0 s, value 0.
Click the timeline lanes halfway across, so the time reads 1.00 / 2.00 s (the playhead line moves there).
Click ◆ Key: a second key appears on the lane at 1 s.
Click that key; under the lanes, type 2.6 in value and press Enter. The arm is up at 1 s.
Press Play above the preview: the arm rises and falls. Add more tracks (Right elbow · bend, Head · turn) the same way.

doItForMe.say: Your new clip is open on the timeline under the preview.
Open + Track… in the timeline tools and pick Right arm · z. A lane appears with a key at 0 s.
At 1 s, ◆ Key, then value 2.6 (and back down at the end): the arm rises and falls as the clip loops.
